round: relevance-filtering research round 16 (zukhruf #3421 follow-up): does a shrinkage recalibration of d1-2B's probability from the reader's taught answers protect the yes/no decisions of an interest whose boundary d1 draws in another place, without making the other interests worse? The last recalibration round (the user, 2026-11-01).
writtenBefore: the seventh fresh slice (2024-07-01..2024-09-30) is prepared, read, answered by d1 or labelled, and before any round-16 score. The Decoder pages of that period are already in fresh-6's crawl store (fresh-6/decoder/articles.sqlite, crawled 2026-10-31; only their publish months were counted, 377 rows); no title, text or answer of them has been read. SiliconANGLE's pages of the period are not crawled yet. fresh-6 (round 15) is used only as a teaching pool here, never as a test.
why: Round 15 (results 93f4a446...) found no gain from shift or platt fitted with Platt's smoothed targets: the frozen product teaching gave no 'no' answer on most profiles (fallback to raw in 16 of 18 pool units), and with random articles the smoothed target of a 'no', 1/(n_not + 2), lies above most of d1's probabilities (67% below 0.05), so the fits pulled the intercepts up (13 of 18 positive) and accepted more false alarms. The one profile where d1's boundary differs from the key, coding (raw accepts 124 to 144 articles for 25 to 28 relevant, T11SU 0), gained 0.000 -> 0.693 from shift. A recalibration's value is protection of such interests, and a topic-level superiority test cannot pass a gain on one of nine profiles (with the other eight exactly at raw the interval is [0.000, +0.231]). Top systems adapt from feedback by starting at the model's own output and moving as the feedback grows (TREC adaptive filtering, CLARIT's beta-gamma thresholding, Zhai et al. TREC-7 1998; Gmail Priority Inbox's per-user model on top of the global model, Aberdeen et al. 2010), and launch with a guardrail plus a positive direction (Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, 2020). The user chose this round to be the last and asked for the realistic option (2026-11-01).

data.test: fresh-7: every the-decoder.com and siliconangle.com article published 2024-07-01..2024-09-30 (UTC). The Decoder rows come from fresh-6's crawl store (the same elt web-source build as fresh-6's 390 Decoder articles); SiliconANGLE is crawled with elt's web source from the post sitemaps that hold posts modified on or after 2024-07-01, keeping only /2024/(07|08|09)/* URLs. Prepared like fresh-6 (every URL and title of the collection and of fresh..fresh-6 excluded). Labelled for all 16 profiles by four blind annotators (Claude, fresh-6's brief word for word; only the paths, queue number and count change, and fresh-6/ is added to the blind list), frozen before any round-16 score. No embeddings are made.
data.answers: d1-2B (LiquidAI/d1-2B-GGUF:Q8_0 on the Mac mini, /v1/systemone, as rounds 13 and 15; model entry and server build recorded) answers every fresh-7 article with round 13's state (title + '\n' + lead) and questions (one noul question per profile, all 16 in one call), frozen (sha256) BEFORE any fresh-7 label exists. A failed call is retried at most 3 times; an article that still fails is recorded and scored as p = 0. The pool's d1 answers are round 15's frozen fresh-6 answers (89855665...).

teaching.arms: Both arms of round 15, unchanged: frozen = round 10's product teaching (per profile, the top N_teach articles of the teaching set by p_d1 and the top N_teach narrow-keyword matches by p_d1); exploration = those articles plus N_teach drawn uniformly at random without replacement from the teaching set's other articles (in teaching-set q order), numpy.random.default_rng([31979, protocol, profile, n_teach]), protocol 0 = window and 1 = pool, profile = its index in profiles.json. The answer key answers each shown article (relevant / not relevant; ambiguous is skipped). N_teach in {5, 10}.
teaching.window: teach from the fresh-7 articles of 2024-07-01..2024-07-14 (UTC publish day), test on the rest of fresh-7.
teaching.pool: teach from fresh-6 (labels 9d8a3e8a..., d1 answers 89855665...), test on all of fresh-7.

calibrations.shift-map: p = logistic(logit(p_d1) + b) with one intercept b per profile, the maximum a posteriori fit under the prior b ~ Normal(0, 1) on the taught answers with hard targets (1 relevant, 0 not relevant): b minimises b^2 / 2 + sum of log losses, which is L2-regularised logistic regression at scikit-learn's and LIBLINEAR's default strength C = 1. Newton with a backtracking line search. p_d1 clipped to [1e-6, 1 - 1e-6] before logit. No smoothed targets.
calibrations.platt-map: p = logistic(a * logit(p_d1) + b) per profile, the maximum a posteriori fit under the prior (a - 1, b) ~ Normal(0, I): (a, b) minimise ((a - 1)^2 + b^2) / 2 + sum of log losses, hard targets, same clipping and solver.
calibrations.fallback: None for shift-map: the prior keeps every fit finite, also when all taught answers are relevant or all are not relevant (such units are counted and reported). A platt-map fit with a <= 0 (it would flatten or reverse the ranking) keeps raw. Both calibrations are monotone otherwise, so the ranking (MAP) of each profile is unchanged; MAP is reported as a check only.

decisions.primary: UtilityThreshold at TREC-11's linear utility T11U = 2 TP - FP, Bayes threshold p >= 1/3 (falseAlarm 1, miss 2), scored by T11SU (T11NU = T11U / (2 * relevant), T11SU = (max(T11NU, -0.5) + 0.5) / 1.5) over the labelled test articles (ambiguous left out). As round 15.
decisions.reported: As round 15: T11F (F0.5) of ExpectedFThreshold(beta 0.5) and of p >= 0.5; Brier skill against the profile's test base rate; expected calibration error (10 equal-width bins); keywordNarrow's T11SU and T11F; MAP of raw d1 (check). Also, per arm, protocol and N_teach: the fitted b (and a), and the units whose taught answers are all relevant or all not relevant.

profiles: Scored profiles: at least 20 strict relevant articles in the test part of each protocol (fresh-7 minus the window for window; all of fresh-7 for pool). Macro means over them. A profile's score of a calibrated condition is the mean over N_teach in {5, 10}.
pass: Topic-level paired bootstrap, 2000 replicates, numpy.random.default_rng(31978), a fresh generator per call. A calibration (shift-map or platt-map) replaces raw in an arm when, in BOTH protocols: (1) guardrail on decisions: the interval of its macro T11SU minus raw's has lower bound > -0.02 (non-inferiority margin: raw d1 led the typed keyword by about 0.19 macro T11SU in round 15, and the margin keeps 90% of that lead, after the FDA's 2016 non-inferiority guidance); (2) guardrail on probabilities: the interval of its macro Brier skill minus raw's has lower bound > -0.05 (round 15's); (3) direction: its macro T11SU minus raw's is > 0 (the point estimate). If both pass, the simpler (shift-map) wins unless platt-map's macro T11SU interval against shift-map lies entirely above 0 in both protocols. The frozen arm's verdict is computed and reported first; the exploration arm is judged on its own by the same rule.
triggered: Reported, not part of the pass rule (Kohavi et al. 2020, triggered analysis): per arm and protocol, the scored profiles in which the calibration accepts a different set of test articles than raw at p >= 1/3 in at least one N_teach, and over them the macro T11SU of the calibration and raw with the interval of the difference (same bootstrap).
then: Frozen arm passes: the chosen calibration becomes a recalibration adapter of the Scorer port (a decorator over DecisionScorer that fits, with the frozen prior, on the interest's own taught answers); its API is shown to the user before it is built. Only the exploration arm passes: the adapter needs the reader to answer some articles that d1 ranks low, so the host must show them; that design and the adapter API are shown to the user before anything is built.
noneEligible: Round 16 is the last recalibration round (the user, 2026-11-01). Thresholds use the decision model's own probability, no recalibration adapter is built, and the research record closes recalibration from taught answers.
